body.title: Send invoice throws TypeError and does nothing on the new invoice page
body.summary: The user created an invoice, saved it as a draft successfully, then clicked "Send invoice" and nothing was sent. The click threw an uncaught TypeError (reading 'id' of undefined) in sendInvoice, and the user rage-clicked the button five times with no change.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the invoices page at app.ledgerly.example/invoices.
Click "New invoice".
The new invoice page (/invoices/new) loads.
Enter a customer in the customer field.
Enter 1250.00 in the amount field.
Click "Save draft".
The draft save request (POST /api/invoices) returns 201.
Click "Send invoice".
A TypeError is thrown in sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21).
An error is logged to the console.
The user clicks "Send invoice" five more times in quick succession (rage click).
The user clicks "Back".

body.expected: Clicking "Send invoice" on a saved draft sends the invoice without a JavaScript error.
body.actual: Clicking "Send invoice" throws an uncaught TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')). The invoice is not sent, the user gets no visible feedback, and repeated clicks have no effect.

evidence.note: Uncaught TypeError thrown in sendInvoice at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21 right after clicking Send invoice.
Matching console error confirms the exception was not handled.
Rage click on #send-invoice (5 clicks) shows the user was stuck and the button was not working.
Draft save returned 201, so the failure happens on the send path after a successful save.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that sendInvoice reads .id from an object that is undefined on the send path, possibly the saved draft or customer reference not being set in state after save.

body.title: Send reminder fails with 500 (reported by [email])
body.summary: On invoice inv_8812, the user clicked "Send reminder" twice, and each click sent a POST to the reminders endpoint. Both requests returned HTTP 500 internal_error and the UI showed "Something went wrong. Please try again." both times.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the invoice page at /invoices/inv_8812.
Click the "Send reminder" button (#send-reminder).
Click the "Send reminder" button (#send-reminder) again.

body.expected: The reminder is sent, or the user sees a clear message explaining why it could not be sent.
body.actual: The reminders POST returns 500 internal_error on each attempt, and the UI shows a generic "Something went wrong" message. The action never succeeds.

evidence.note: First POST to /api/invoices/inv_8812/reminders returns 500 internal_error (request_id req_7Hk2).
The UI shows the generic error message right after the first failed request.
Retry POST returns 500 internal_error again (request_id req_7Hm9), so the failure is repeatable.
The generic error message appears again, and the user gets no actionable detail.

body.suspected_cause: A server-side exception in the reminders endpoint is likely failing for inv_8812, since the 500 is returned consistently and no client-side errors were logged.

body.title: AR aging report times out (504 gateway_timeout) for 90d range on /reports
body.summary: User opened the AR aging report, which requested the 90-day range and waited about 30 seconds before the gateway returned a 504 gateway_timeout. They then rage-clicked the report link and saw a message suggesting a shorter range.

Click the 'AR aging' link (#aging-report)
Wait for the aging report to load with the 90-day range
Click the #aging-report element repeatedly (4 clicks)
Read the message shown on the page

body.expected: The AR aging report loads for the 90-day range within a reasonable time.
body.actual: The request GET /api/reports/aging?range=90d returns 504 with gateway_timeout after about 30 seconds, and the UI shows 'This report is taking too long. Try a shorter range.'

evidence.note: Aging request for range=90d returned 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms.
User rage-clicked the report link 4 times while waiting, indicating the page appeared unresponsive.
UI displayed a timeout message suggesting a shorter range, so the report never loaded.

body.suspected_cause: The aging report backend likely exceeds the gateway timeout (about 30 seconds) when querying the 90-day range, possibly due to slow query or missing optimization for large date ranges.

body.title: Payments page fails to load: lazy chunk 812 returns 404 after deploy
body.summary: The user opened the dashboard and clicked Payments, which navigated to /payments. The lazy-loaded chunk 812 returned 404, triggering a ChunkLoadError and a 'Page failed to load.' message.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the dashboard at app.ledgerly.example/dashboard.
Click the Payments nav link (#nav-payments).
The app navigates to /payments and begins loading the Payments route.

body.expected: The Payments page loads and displays normally.
body.actual: The request for /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returns 404, a ChunkLoadError is thrown in lazyPayments, and the page shows 'Page failed to load.' The user clicks Reload.

evidence.note: Chunk 812 request returns 404, meaning the hashed asset is missing on the server.
ChunkLoadError thrown from lazyPayments in routes.tsx, showing the route failed on its lazy import.
UI shows 'Page failed to load.' so the user sees a broken page with no recovery path.
User clicks Reload, which is the only recovery action taken in the session.

body.suspected_cause: The client is likely running stale bundle references from a previous build after the 2026.10.27-1 deploy, so the old chunk hash no longer exists on the server.

body.title: Customer CSV export returns 500 and client logs expose customer email and session token
body.summary: The user searched for a customer by email, typed a card number into the page, and clicked Export CSV, which showed 'Export failed.' The export request returned HTTP 500 with export_failed, and the console logged the customer's email along with a session token.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the customers page with the search query set to a customer's email address.
Wait while the page loads; the console logs a debug message containing the customer's email and a session token.
Enter '4242 4242 4242 4242' into the card number field (#card-number).
Click the Export CSV button (#export-csv).
The app sends GET /api/customers/export with the customer's email in the query string and receives a 500 response.
The console logs an error that includes the customer's email and the 500 status.
The page shows the message 'Export failed.'

body.expected: The CSV export completes and downloads, and customer email, session tokens, and card data are not written to logs or put in URLs.
body.actual: The export fails with HTTP 500 (export_failed). Customer email and a session token are written to the console and the email appears in the export URL.

evidence.note: At 800 ms the console logs the customer email with a session token, exposing credentials and PII in client logs.
At 5300 ms the export GET returns 500 and carries the customer email in the query string, which can leak into logs and history.
At 6240 ms the error log repeats the customer email, confirming PII is logged on failure.
At 3000 ms a full card number is typed into the page during an export flow, so card data is captured in the recording.

body.suspected_cause: The export endpoint likely fails with a server-side 500 for this request, and client code likely logs the full request context including the email and session token, which would also explain the PII in the URL.

body.title: Revenue report shows error with RangeError when applying invalid date 2026-02-30 in date range picker
body.summary: The user opened the revenue report, entered the nonexistent date 2026-02-30 in the date-from field, and clicked Apply. The app threw an unhandled RangeError in formatDateRange, showed 'Something went wrong loading this report.', and the user rage-clicked Apply six times.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Navigate to the revenue report at /reports/revenue with the default 30-day range.
Click the 'Date range' control.
Enter 2026-02-30 in the date-from field.
Click 'Apply'.
Click 'Apply' repeatedly (six times in quick succession).

body.expected: The date picker should reject an invalid date like 2026-02-30 with a validation message, or clamp it to a valid date, and keep the report usable.
body.actual: An uncaught RangeError ('Invalid time value') is thrown in formatDateRange, the console logs the error, the report displays a generic failure message, and the user repeatedly clicks Apply.

evidence.note: Revenue report loads successfully with the default 30-day range before any user input.
The invalid date value 2026-02-30 is entered into the date-from field.
Uncaught RangeError 'Invalid time value' thrown at formatDateRange in DateRangePicker.tsx, called from RevenueChart.
Matching console error is logged, confirming the exception is unhandled.
User sees 'Something went wrong loading this report.' instead of an input validation message.
Six rage clicks on Apply show the user is stuck and the control is not recovering.

body.suspected_cause: The date range input likely isn't validated before formatDateRange parses it, so an impossible date like 2026-02-30 produces an Invalid Date that throws a RangeError.

User retries the payment and the same button and endpoint are used.

draft.suspected_cause: The Paylane payment provider likely had a temporary outage, and the app's error handling appears to have worked as designed.

draft.title: Search returns no results for misspelled invoice query 'invocie 1042' (no typo tolerance, works as designed)
draft.summary: The user searched the invoices page for 'invocie 1042' and got a 'No invoices match' message. They corrected the query to 'invoice 1042', got the invoice, and opened INV-1042 within about 7 seconds.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the invoices page at app.ledgerly.example/invoices.
Type 'invocie 1042' into the #search field.
The search request for q=invocie+1042 returns 200 in about 70 ms.
The page shows 'No invoices match invocie 1042'.
Change the search text to 'invoice 1042'.
The search request for q=invoice+1042 returns 200 in about 75 ms.
Click the row INV-1042 in the results.

draft.expected: Searching for a term with a typo returns no results, which is expected because the search does exact or substring matching and has no typo tolerance. The user then corrects the spelling and finds the invoice.
draft.actual: The misspelled query returned no matches, the user corrected it, and the correct query returned INV-1042, which they opened. The search and navigation worked as designed.

evidence.note: The UI shows 'No invoices match' for the misspelled query, with a 200 response, so the empty result is correct for that input.
The user retyped the query with the correct spelling, which indicates they recognized the typo themselves.
The user clicked INV-1042 after the corrected search, so the correct query returned the expected result.

draft.suspected_cause: The search appears to match the literal query text without typo tolerance or 'did you mean' suggestions, so a misspelling yields no results, which is likely a usability gap rather than a defect.

draft.title: Past due date rejected on draft invoice save (expected validation, not a bug)
draft.summary: The user entered a due date of 2026-10-01, which is before the session date, and clicked Save draft. The server returned a 422 with 'Due date must be today or later', the UI showed that message, and the user changed the date to 2026-11-15 and saved successfully.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the new invoice page at /invoices/new.
Enter 2026-10-01 in the due date field.
Click Save draft.
Server rejects the POST to /api/invoices with a 422 validation error on due_date.
The page displays 'Due date must be today or later'.
Change the due date to 2026-11-15.
Click Save draft again.
The POST to /api/invoices returns 201 and the draft is saved.

draft.expected: A due date in the past is rejected with a clear message, and a valid future date saves the draft.
draft.actual: The past date was rejected with the expected message, and the later valid date saved the draft with a 201 response.

evidence.note: Server returns 422 on due_date with the message 'Due date must be today or later', confirming server-side validation fired.
UI shows the same validation message, so the user received feedback about the error.
Retry with 2026-11-15 returns 201, showing the save path works once the date is valid.

draft.suspected_cause: Likely no defect: the server's due date validation is working as designed and the user corrected the input on their own.

per_recording.category: missing or undefined data in client-side routing

draft.title: View customer link on invoice page requests /api/customers/undefined and shows 'Customer not found.'
draft.summary: On invoice inv_6620, the user clicked 'View customer' to open the customer's record. The app requested /api/customers/undefined, got a 404, and showed 'Customer not found.' instead.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the invoice page at /invoices/inv_6620.
Click the 'View customer' button.

draft.expected: Clicking 'View customer' opens the customer record linked to invoice inv_6620.
draft.actual: The app calls GET /api/customers/undefined, which returns 404 not_found, and displays 'Customer not found.'

evidence.note: The 'View customer' click is the only user action in the recording, so the failing request follows directly from it.
The request URL contains the literal string 'undefined' where the customer ID should be, so the ID was missing when the link was built.
The user sees a 'Customer not found.' message, although the customer exists and the failure comes from the bad ID.

draft.suspected_cause: The invoice page likely passes an undefined customer ID to the 'View customer' link, possibly because the invoice payload lacks a customer_id field or the frontend reads the wrong property name.

judge.reason: The title, steps, and expected versus actual behavior accurately capture the failure. However, the evidence references are mismatched: E1 is the network request, E2 is the UI message, and E3 does not exist in the timeline. The claim that the customer exists is unsupported, as is the assertion that the ID was missing when the link was built.

draft.title: Payments table crashes on Refunds filter: null amount in formatRow
draft.summary: User loaded the payments page, which fetched all payments successfully, then clicked the Refunds filter. The click triggered a TypeError reading 'amount' from null in PaymentsTable.tsx, and the page showed 'Something went wrong.'

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the payments page at app.ledgerly.example/payments.
Wait for the payments list to load with status=all (returned 200).
Click the Refunds filter.

draft.expected: The table filters to refund payments and renders them.
draft.actual: A TypeError (Cannot read properties of null, reading 'amount') is thrown in formatRow, and the UI shows 'Something went wrong.'

evidence.note: Uncaught TypeError in formatRow (PaymentsTable.tsx:77) shortly after the Refunds click, indicating a row with a null value is being formatted.
Generic error message replaces the table, so the user cannot see the refund results.

draft.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that formatRow does not guard against a null payment or amount field for refund records, so the filtered rows crash the render.

judge.reason: The report captures the two observed actions, exception, and error message, and the title is specific. However, the hostname, successful status=all fetch, and HTTP 200 are not in the timeline. The evidence also does not establish that the message replaced the table or that a refund record or its amount field was null; the exception only establishes that 'amount' was read from a null value.
